doubles-triples.name: Doubles Triples
doubles-triples.description: Practice tests for the Doubles Triples endorsement

questions.question: You should check the height of the trailer before connecting a converter dolly to a second or third trailer. The trailer height is right when:
options: The trailer will be raised slightly when the converter dolly is backed under it.
The center of the kingpin lines up with the locking jaws
The kingpin rests on the fifth wheel
questions.explanation: Make sure trailer height is correct. It must be slightly lower than the center of the fifth wheel, so trailer is raised slightly when dolly is pushed under.

questions.question: The best way to stop all skids is to:
options: Restore traction to the tires
Use stab or controlled braking
Counter steer and accelerate
questions.explanation: When any vehicle starts to skid, you must act to restore traction to the wheels.

questions.question: When does the drivers manual advise disconnecting the steering axle brakes to help keep the rig straight?
options: Any time you must
Never
When the road is dry
questions.explanation: You should never disconnect the steering axel brakes.

questions.question: When driving with more than one trailer, which trailer should be the first one behind the tractor?
options: The shortest trailer
The heaviest trailer
The lightest trailer
questions.explanation: For the safest handling on the road, the more heavily loaded semitrailer should be in first position behind the tractor. The lighter trailer should be in the rear.

questions.question: Driving a truck with double or triple trailers requires a driver to:
options: Allow more following distance than for smaller vehicles
Use special care in bad weather and mountain conditions
Do both things
questions.explanation: Be more careful in adverse conditions like bad weather, slippery conditions, and mountain driving, you must be especially careful if you drive double and triple trailers. You will have greater length and more dead axles to pull with your drive axles than other drivers. There is more chance for skids and loss of traction.

questions.question: Which of these will result in the best control on curves?
options: Braking during the turn
Slowing to a safe speed before entering the curve, then accelerate slightly during the curve
Downshift after you enter the curve
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed, and downshift to the right gear before entering the curve. This lets you use some power through the curve to help the vehicle be more stable while turning.

questions.question: You are driving a 100' vehicle with double trailers at 30 MPH. The road is dry, and visibility is good. You should keep at least _____ seconds of space ahead of you:
questions.explanation: One good rule says you need at least one second for each 10 feet of vehicle length at speeds below 40 mph. At greater speeds, you must add 1 second for safety.

questions.question: You are driving with double trailers and must use your brakes to avoid a crash. For emergency braking you should:
options: Push the brake pedal as hard as you can and hold it there
Use controlled or stab braking
Use only the trailer brakes
questions.explanation: You should brake in a way that will keep your vehicle in a straight line and allow you to turn if it becomes necessary. You can use the controlled braking method or the stab braking method.

questions.question: You are doing a walk around inspection of a double or triple trailer rig. You should be sure the converter dolly air tank drain valves are _____ and the pintle hook is _____.
options: Open, free
Closed, latched
Open, latched
questions.explanation: Converter dolly air tank drain valve are closed, and make sure pintle hook is latched.

questions.question: A converter dolly is
options: an electronic device that connects the electric power from a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer.
a coupling device that connects a semitrailer to the rear of a tractor-trailer.
a coupling device that converts the electricity between a semitrailer and a tractor-trailer for international trucking.
questions.explanation: A converter gear on a dolly is a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor trailer combination forming a double bottom rig.

questions.question: If a converter dolly has spring brakes, you release the brakes by
options: opening the air tank petcock.
using the dolly's parking brake control.
doing both of the above.
questions.explanation: Release dolly brakes by opening the air tank petcock, or, if the dolly has spring brakes, use the dolly parking brake control.

questions.question: You have connected the converter dolly to the front semitrailer and then connected the rear semitrailer to the converter dolly. How should you test the coupling?
options: Pull against the rear semitrailer's pin.
Drive forward, brake suddenly, and see if the rear semitrailer hits the one in front of it.
Drive forward slowly and see if the rear semitrailer stays attached.
questions.explanation: Test coupling by pulling against pin of the rear semitrailer

questions.question: To test the tractor protection valve, charge the trailer air brake system, turn off the engine, and
options: flash your high-beam headlights on and off several times.
keep pressing the brake pedal firmly.
step on and off the brake pedal several times.
questions.explanation: Charge the trailer air brake system. Shut the engine off. Step on and off the brake pedal several times to reduce the air pressure in the tanks. The trailer air supply control should pop out or go from "normal" to "emergency" position when the air pressure falls into the pressure range specified by the manufacturer. Usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi.

questions.question: If your landing gear is power operated, you should check for ________ during your walk-around inspection.
options: leaks of water or gasoline
dirt or grime
leaks of air or hydraulic fluid
questions.explanation: If the landing gear is power operated, make sure there are no air or hydraulic leaks.

questions.question: Coupling a triple trailer is different from coupling other combinations because
options: you couple the third trailer to the second trailer before you couple them to the first trailer.
you do not have to use a converter dolly.
you couple the second trailer to the first trailer and then couple them both to the tractor.
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle has four units (not counting the converter dollies): a tractor and three trailers. You couple a triple as follows: 1. Couple the first trailer to the tractor the same way that you couple any combination vehicle. 2. Couple the third trailer to the second trailer using the method for coupling doubles (which will involve the use of a converter dolly). 3. Move another converter dolly into position. 3. Couple the tractor and first trailer to the second and third trailer using the method for coupling doubles (which will involve another converter dolly).

questions.question: The tractor protection valve is designed to close automatically when the air pressure falls into the pressure range specified by the manufacturer, typically
options: 75 to 100 psi.
20 to 45 psi.
50 to 75 psi.
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control should pop out or go from "normal" to "emergency" position when the air pressure falls into the pressure range specified by the manufacturer. Usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi.

questions.question: In order, the four steps to test your trailer's service brakes are as follows
options: Check for normal air pressure. Release the parking brakes. Pull forward slowly. Apply the trailer brakes, using the hand control if so equipped.
Apply the trailer brakes, using the hand control if so equipped. Release the trailer's parking brakes. Check for normal air pressure. Pull forward slowly.
Check for normal air pressure. Release the parking brakes. Apply the trailer brakes, using the hand control if so equipped. Step off the brakes and pull forward slowly.
questions.explanation: Wait for normal air pressure, release the parking brake, move the vehicle forward slowly about five mph, and apply the brakes firmly using the trailers hand control. Note any vehicle pulling to one side, unusual feel, or delayed stopping action.

questions.question: If your test of the tractor protection valve is successful,
options: the tractor protection valve control (trailer air supply control) will pop out or go from "normal" to "emergency."
the parking brake valve will pop out.
the low air pressure warning signal will come on.
questions.explanation: The trailer air supply control also called the tractor protection valve control should pop out or go from "normal" to "emergency" position when the air pressure falls into the pressure range specified by the manufacturer usually within the range of 20 to 45 psi.

questions.question: To uncouple the rear trailer, the first thing you do is
options: park the vehicle in a straight line on firm level ground.
park the vehicle at a 45-degree angle on an incline.
park the vehicle at a 45-degree angle on level ground.
questions.explanation: Park rig in a straight line on firm level ground.

questions.question: A converter dolly with antilock brakes (ABS) is required to have
options: a yellow lamp on the left side.
a white lamp on the right side.
a white lamp on the left side.
questions.explanation: Converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998, are required to have antilock brakes. These dollies will have a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly.

questions.question: You are driving a 100-foot twin trailer combination at 50 mph. The road is dry, and visibility is good. You should keep at least _____ seconds of space ahead of you.
questions.explanation: One good rule says you need at least one second for each 10 feet of vehicle length at speeds below 40 mph. At greater speeds, you must add 1 second for safety.

questions.question: You are driving a 100-foot twin trailer combination at 50 mph. The road is dry, and visibility is good. You should keep at least _____ seconds of space ahead of you.
questions.explanation: The convex mirrors are located below the outside flat mirrors. They are used to monitor the left and right sides at a wide angle. They provide a view of traffic and clearances. These mirrors present a view of people and objects that does not accurately reflect their size and distance.

questions.question: Some large trucks have convex or spot mirrors.
options: Are against the law in most states
Make things look smaller and farther away than the really are
Do not need to be checked as often as flat mirrors because they show a larger area
questions.explanation: The convex mirrors are located below the outside flat mirrors. They are used to monitor the left and right sides at a wide angle. They provide a view of traffic and clearances. These mirrors present a view of people and objects that does not accurately reflect their size and distance.

questions.question: Which of these statements about managing space to the sides is true?
options: Always keep your vehicle to the right side of your lane
High winds are not a problem for doubles and triples
You should avoid traveling next to others when possible
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles are often wide and take up most of a lane. Safe drivers will manage what little space they have. You can do this by keeping your vehicle centered in your lane and avoid driving alongside others.

questions.question: Which of these statements about handling of doubles and triples is true?
options: A triple rig can stop quicker than a 5-axle tractor semi-trailer due to off tracking
The rear trailer of a 100-foot triple is less likely to turn over than a single semi-trailer due to the crack the whip effect
A sudden movement with the steering wheel can result in a tipped over rear trailer
questions.explanation: To prevent trailers from rolling over, you must steer gently and go slowly around corners, on ramps, off ramps, and curves. A safe speed on a curve for a straight truck or a single trailer combination vehicle may be too fast for a set of doubles or triples.

questions.question: When should you check your mirrors while making a lane change?
options: After signaling the change
Right after starting the lane change
After completing the lane change
All answers are correct
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors: Before you change lanes to make sure there is enough room. After you have signaled, to check that no one has moved into your blind spot. Right after you start the lane change, to doublecheck that your path is clear. After you complete the lane change.

questions.question: Before you can supply air to the air tanks of a second trailer you need to:
options: Close the shut off valves at the rear of both trailers
Open the shut off valves at the rear of both trailers
Open the shut off valves at the rear of the first trailer, and close the shut off valves at the rear of the second trailer
questions.explanation: Shut-off valves at rear of trailers, in service and emergency lines. Rear of front trailers: open. Rear of last trailer: closed.

questions.question: If you must drive through deep puddles or flowing water, which of these should you not do?
options: Use a lower gear
Increase engine rpm
Drive though quickly
Gently pressing the brake pedal while driving through the water.
questions.explanation: Slow down and place transmission in a low gear. Gently put on the brakes. This presses linings against brake drums or discs and keeps mud, silt, sand, and water from getting in.

questions.question: During an inspection of a double or triple combination, check the usual things for any combination vehicle and check
options: the fifth wheel and the landing gear.
the trailers and the radios in the tractor.
the shut-off valves, the converter dolly or dollies, and the air brakes on all trailers.
questions.explanation: To inspect a double or triple, first inspect it just as you would inspect any combination vehicle. Then check that the shut-off valves are open on all trailers but the last trailer. Check each converter dolly to be sure that the pintle hook is properly latched.

questions.question: When you pull two or three trailers, you should look farther ahead because
options: aggressive drivers may cause trouble for you on the road.
the vehicle is more likely to roll over or jackknife.
both of the above are true.
questions.explanation: Doubles and triples must be driven very smoothly to avoid rollover or jackknife. Therefore, look far ahead so you can slow down or change lanes gradually when necessary.

questions.question: If you want to couple a second trailer to your combination vehicle, secure it by using?
options: The trailers spring brakes and emergency air brakes
Wheel chocks
Either answer can be correct
questions.explanation: Make sure trailer brakes are locked and/or wheels chocked.

questions.question: Which of these statements about quick steering movements and doubles / triples is true?
options: Doubles / triples flip over from quick steering movement easier than many other vehicles
You should put on the brakes at the same time you perform quick steering movements
Counter steering is easier with doubles / triples than with most other vehicles
questions.explanation: Rearward amplification causes the crack-the-whip effect. Triples have a rearward amplification of 3.5 meaning you can roll the last trailer of triples 3.5 times as easily as a five-axle tractor. A Double has a reward amplification of 2 being twice as likely to roll over as a five-axel trailer.

questions.question: The best way to keep brakes from overheating while going down a steep grade is to:
options: Use only the trailer brakes
Go 5 MPH below your safe speed
Use stab braking
questions.explanation: The use of brakes on a long and/or steep downgrade is only a supplement to the braking effect of the engine. The following are the proper braking techniques: Apply the brakes just hard enough to feel a definite slowdown. When your speed has been reduced to approximately five mph below your "safe" speed, release the brakes. When your speed has increased to your "safe" speed, repeat.

questions.question: Converter dollies:
options: Often do not have spring brakes
Have little braking power because they are small
Usually need a glad hand converter
questions.explanation: Converter dollies often do not have spring brakes.

questions.question: You are driving a set of doubles, and a set of trailer wheels goes into a skid. Which of these is most likely to occur?
options: The rig will continue to move in a straight line no matter how much the steering wheel is turned
The rig will stay in a straight line but slide sideways
A trailer jackknife
questions.explanation: Doubles and triples must be driven very smoothly to avoid rollover or jackknife. Therefore, look far ahead so you can slow down or change lanes gradually when necessary.

questions.question: Antilock brakes (ABS) have been required on all converter dollies built since
options: March 2000.
March 1998.
March 2003.
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes built on or after March 1, 1997 require ABS, and other air brake vehicles such as trucks, buses, trailers, and converter dollies built on or after March 1, 1998 require ABS.

questions.question: Why must you inspect your double or triple combination vehicle more extensively than a vehicle with only one such semitrailer?
options: Its design makes it more likely to have problems.
There are more critical parts to check.
The types of cargoes it carries make it more likely to have problems.
questions.explanation: There are more things to inspect on a double or triple combination vehicle than on a single vehicle. Many of these items are simply more of what you would find on a single vehicle. For example, tires, wheels, lights, reflectors, etc. However, there are also some new things to check.

questions.question: Which of these statements about seeing ahead is true?
options: At highway speed you should look up to 1/4 mile ahead of your truck
Good drivers shift their attention back and forth, near and far
Many drivers do not look far enough ahead of their truck
All answers are correct
questions.explanation: Most good drivers look at least 12 to 15 seconds ahead. That means looking ahead the distance you will travel in 12 to 15 seconds. At lower speeds, that's about one block. At highway speeds it's about a quarter of a mile.

questions.question: The crack the whip effects trucks with trailers. Which of the following is most likely to tip over?
options: The rear trailer of a triple
The rear trailer of a double
A full trailer behind a truck
questions.explanation: Due to rearward amplification a double is twice as likely, and a triple is 3.5 times more likely to roll over than a five-axel trailer.

questions.question: A converter dolly consists of a ______ wheel and ________ axles.
options: fifth; two or three
third; two or three
fifth; one or two
questions.explanation: A converter gear on a dolly is a coupling device of one or two axles and a fifth wheel by which a semitrailer can be coupled to the rear of a tractor trailer combination forming a double bottom rig.

questions.question: The first step in uncoupling a converter dolly is
options: to disconnect the safety chains.
to slowly pull clear of it.
to lower its landing gear.
questions.explanation: Lower dolly landing gear.

questions.question: How can you be sure you supplied air to a second trailer?
options: Go to the rear of the second trailer and open the emergency line shut off
Watch each trailers air gauge for a drop of 30 PSI
Apply the hand valve at 10 MPH, you should stop in the same distance as a truck with one trailer at 5 MPH
questions.explanation: Use the tractor parking brake and/or chock the wheels to hold the vehicle. Wait for air pressure to reach normal, then push in the red "trailer air supply" knob. This will supply air to the emergency (supply) lines. Open the emergency line shut-off valve at the rear of the last trailer. You should hear air escaping, showing the entire system is charged.

questions.question: If a converter dolly is still under the second trailer and you unlock the pintle hook, what will probably happen?
options: The trailer brakes will unlock
The airlines will rupture
The dolly tow bar may fly up
questions.explanation: Never unlock the pintle hook with the dolly still under the rear trailer. The dolly tow bar may fly up, possibly causing injury, and making it very difficult to re-couple.

questions.question: If a converter dolly is still under the second trailer and you unlock the pintle hook, what will probably happen?
options: The trailer brakes will unlock
The airlines will rupture
The dolly tow bar may fly up
questions.explanation: Check that the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate with no gap.

questions.question: You are visually checking the coupling of a converter dolly to the rear trailer. How much space should be between the upper and lower fifth wheel?
options: It depends on the load
None
1/2 to 3/4 inch
questions.explanation: Check that the trailer is lying flat on the fifth wheel skid plate with no gap.

questions.question: When you uncouple twin trailers, the last step is to
options: uncouple the converter dolly.
release the brakes on the converter dolly.
slowly pull clear of the converter dolly.
questions.explanation: Slowly pull clear of dolly.

questions.question: Converter dollies
options: have little braking power because they are small.
sometimes do not have antilock brakes.
usually need a glad hand converter.
questions.explanation: All converter dollies built since 1998 are required to have antilock brakes.

questions.question: You want to hook your combination to a second trailer that has no spring brakes. To do this without wheel chocks you should:
options: Supply air to the trailer air system with the tractor and then disconnect the emergency line
Make sure the trailer will roll freely when coupling
Hook the trailer electric cord to a portable generator for braking power
questions.explanation: If the second trailer doesn't have spring brakes, drive the tractor close to the trailer, connect the emergency line, charge the trailer air tank, and disconnect the emergency line. This will set the trailer emergency brakes if the slack adjusters are correctly adjusted.

questions.question: Empty trucks:
options: Require shorter stopping distances than full ones.
May have poor traction due to bouncing and wheel lockup
Are the easiest to stop since there is no shifting cargo
questions.explanation: Empty trucks require greater stopping distances because an empty vehicle has less traction.

questions.question: When parking your double or triple combination, you should look for a parking space
options: that you can pull straight through.
that is as close as possible to your destination.
that you can back out of.
questions.explanation: Make sure you do not get in a spot you cannot pull straight through. You need to be aware of how parking lots are arranged to avoid a long and difficult escape.

questions.question: With the hand valve on, you should test the trailer brakes by opening the service line valve at the rear of the rig. When you do this, you should hear:
options: The emergency line valve open and release air
The service brakes slowly move to the fully applied position
Air escapes from the open valve
questions.explanation: Open the service line valve, listen for air to escape, and then close the valve.

questions.question: Which of these in not a good thing to do when driving on slippery roads?
options: Use the engine brake or speed retarder
Keep other traffic out of you side space
Use a light touch on the accelerator and brake pedals
questions.explanation: When your drive wheels have poor traction, the retarder may cause them to skid. Therefore, you should turn the retarder off whenever the road is wet, icy, or snow covered.

questions.question: Double and triple combination vehicles are ________ stable than other types of commercial vehicles.
options: less
more
neither more nor less
questions.explanation: Take special care when pulling two and three trailers. There are more things that can go wrong, and doubles/triples are less stable than other commercial vehicles.
